correctness.rationale: For all k>=2, build the overlap digraph on binary (k-1)-words of weight <=2, with a labeled edge for each k-word of weight <=2. The graph is balanced and strongly connected, and a unique zero-word self-loop fixes the starting rotation. The fixed-first-edge BEST/last-exit theorem counts cycles by rooted directed in-arborescences; since all outdegrees are 1 or 2, local factorials are 1. Weight-2 vertices have forced shift-plus-zero edges. Contracting their paths leaves each singleton index j=0..m-1 (m=k-1) with Z(j)=j-1 (0 maps to root) or O(j)=m-1-j. If low j<=floor((m-1)/2) selects O, the nonempty interval [j,m-1-j] is forward invariant, forbidding root access. If all lows select Z, either choice at every high j decreases index and reaches root; highs are independent. There are floor(m/2) high indices, giving U_k=2^floor((k-1)/2). Each cycle has k ones by double-counting the total factor weight k+2C(k,2)=k^2. Independent index-choice exhaustive calculation checked k=2..14, not the full theorem.
residual_risks: Finite independent computations are diagnostic only for quantified unbounded theorems; correctness relies on the reconstructed proof.

value.rationale: This gives a complete all-k enumeration and canonical Boolean-cube bijection of the entire natural set of rotation classes of weight-[0,2] binary universal cycles. Existence and generic BEST machinery were known; evaluating and classifying every tour for a meaningful constrained language is a standalone nontrivial enumeration, useful as a benchmark for random generation and higher-weight work.
